thread:
Maria (runtime): quick sync — running a small probe to "stitch" FlashAttn v2/v3 into the kernel chooser. saw weird KV-cache regen on short seqs; want an ops window to run a safe canary.
Liang: can you paste the tiny repro and the numbers you saw?
Maria (runtime): repro command:```./run_bench --model=redwood-compat --seq=32 --batch=16 --kernel_probe=1```
Maria (runtime): baseline: p50=18ms, throughput=1250 qps. probe run: p50=27ms, throughput=1100 qps (≈12% drop). kernel chooser log:```[chooser] seq=32 -> selected=fa_v3 (score=0.73) ; fallback=fa_v2 (score=0.70) ; kv_state=regen```
Jonathan: interesting — I remember a similar blip where short seqs got grouped with long ones, forcing paged-KV warmups. could be batching heuristic.
Maria (runtime): traced it down: our bucketing does `bucket = floor(seq/16)`, so seq=32 and seq=48 end up same bucket when combined with padding in autobatcher. that mixes short and medium sequences and triggers fa_v3 path which assumes warmed KV.
Liang: ah. so two issues: kernel score calc doesn't consider recent kv_hit_rate, and autobatcher bucketing amplifies mixing.
Maria (runtime): exact. proposed minimal change:```
- bucket_stride = 16
+ bucket_stride = 8
+ if seq < 64 and kv_hit_rate < 0.95: prefer fa_v2
```
Siggi: ops ask — want to canary this tonight. recommended flow: 1) patch chooser to consider kv_hit_rate, 2) reduce bucket_stride to 8, 3) deploy to canary group (fflag=fa_kernel_mux=canary:5%), 4) run perf-bot sweep, 5) observe error/latency for 2 hours, then ramp.
Maria (runtime): agree. fflag snippet we'll use:```{"name":"fa_kernel_mux","variants":{"control":95,"fa_v3_pref":5}}``` planning us-east-1 first.
perf-bot: running micro-bench (1k queries across seq=[8,16,32,48,96])... results:```
control: p50=19ms p95=42ms tput=1240
canary:  p50=20ms p95=29ms tput=1210
notes: short-seq p50 delta +1ms, but p95 improved by ~13ms (less regen tail)
```
Jonathan: those perf-bot numbers look ok — less tail which is good. small p50 bump expected from more conservative bucketing.
Liang: also add a metric: `kv_cache_hit_rate_by_bucket` so we can drive chooser decisions from real telemetry.
Maria (runtime): will add that to the tracing payload. rollout timeline: patch -> canary 5% (2h) -> if green ramp 20% (1h) -> full. rollback condition: p95 > control p95 * 1.15 or error rate spike > 0.1%.
Siggi: ops scheduled 23:00 PST. tagging oncall. @ops-bot can you reserve the window?
ops-bot: reserved 23:00-01:00 PST; will run auto-rollback if p95 threshold hit. :white_check_mark:
Maria (runtime): thanks — I'll open the PR and attach the fflag change + perf graphs. ping if you want to join the monitoring session. :thumbsup:
Jonathan: i'll watch dashboards during canary.
Liang: +1, will add kv_hit_rate panels.
perf-bot: bench post-canary (500q): canary p95=28ms (control 42ms) ; cpu util difference +2% on serving nodes.
Maria (runtime): final note: this is a narrow fix (chooser + bucketing). still plan a follow-up to refine kernel scoring to include estimated cold_kv_penalty as a first-class term.
Siggi: sounds good. thanks team.
